title: The Pose It Cannot Hold: Asking an Arm Its Question in Both Directions, and Telling the Pose It Cannot Reach From the One It Cannot Take or Hold

questions.question: An arm fails to go to a pose. What are the three reasons, and are the remedies the same?
options: Out of reach, outside the joint limits, too heavy to hold: three remedies
questions.explanation: The planner gave four different verdicts for four targets.

questions.question: Which is tested first, and why?
options: Out of reach: with no angles there is nothing to check the limits or torques of
questions.explanation: The wrist has to be reachable before anything else means anything.

questions.question: The arm straight out, payload 0.5 kg. Which motor is nearest its limit?
questions.explanation: The shoulder carries the whole arm.

questions.question: A payload of 0.801648 kg at the pose straight out. What is true of the shoulder?
options: It is at its limit: 80 of 80 N m

questions.question: Two ways of reaching a pose, both legal and both holdable. Which does the plan take?
options: The one with the lower torque
The quicker from where the arm is
questions.explanation: It took the elbow up from near the elbow up way and down from near the other.

questions.question: Why is the torque a static check only?
options: It is the torque to hold still: moving asks more, which lesson 13-07 is about
questions.explanation: The lesson says so under what it does not do.
